name: Prasonisi
notes: Sandbar isthmus with two sides: waves on the west side, flatter lagoon on the east side (the wind is stronger and steadier there). Meltemi (NW) May–Sept, strongest July–Aug, a few knots above the rest of Rhodes; crowded in season. Schools teach on the lagoon, but one local site says kiting is restricted on the flat side: check the rules on the spot.

name: Marmari
notes: North-west coast of Kos, accelerated between the islands offshore: thermal meltemi (NW) from about noon to sunset, strong from June to September. Waist-deep sandbank about 50 m out, chop to small waves on windy days. The permitted kite zone is downwind where the beach is narrow with trees: tricky launch and landing. Several kite centres.

name: Psalidi
notes: North-east coast of Kos east of Kos Town, beach faces the strait to Turkey: side-onshore meltemi (N), strongest in the afternoon, shallow beginner-friendly water with chop. Kite centre on the beach, season May to October.

name: Afiartis – Makry Gialos
notes: Three bays near the airport (Chicken Bay for learning, Gun Bay, Devil's Bay): very strong and consistent meltemi from the north, over low land, flat water. A tour operator reports that kiting is not allowed in the bays while the windsurf centres are open (about 9:00–19:00): check locally. The dedicated kite beach is reported to be Agrilaopotamos, a few km away.

name: Mikri Vigla
notes: Meltemi (N), May–Sep, funnelled between Naxos and Paros: side-onshore, flat-ish water. A rocky headland splits the beach: kite on the north side, swimmers on the south. Narrow beach and rocky cape: some experience needed. Several IKO schools on site.

name: Pounta
notes: Channel towards Antiparos: the meltemi (N) is accelerated through the 1 km strait; flat in the shallows, choppy when it blows hard; current in the channel. Two kite centres; watch the Paros–Antiparos ferry route. Also: Golden Beach / New Golden Beach on the east coast (meltemi side-shore, chop; mainly windsurf).

name: Korfos
notes: North-west bay: the meltemi (N) is funnelled by the hills, strong late June to early September, gusty above 30 kt. Not very wide: ride upwind for space. Kite school on the beach; crowded in season.

name: Keros
notes: Wide bay on the east coast of Lemnos: flat water on the north side, small chop in the middle, a wave in the south when the meltemi (N) is strong. Meltemi June to September, peak July–August; beginners do best in June and early July. Surf Club Keros (IKO, open May to mid October) sits in the middle of the bay; a second kite centre also operates here.

name: Lefkada – Agios Ioannis
notes: Beach north of Lefkada town (also called Milos beach), by the windmills: afternoon NW thermal (maistro), April to September, onshore with small waves. A line of yellow buoys splits the beach: windsurf on one side, kite on the other. The kite school and Myloi (a kite-only beach next door) are here. This is Lefkada's kite spot: sources say kiting is prohibited at Vassiliki all year.

name: Kouremenos (Palaikastro)
notes: Beach 5 km east of Palekastro, far east Crete: funnelled meltemi (N–NW), side-offshore and gusty, thermal build-up from midday (20–30 kt in June–August); flat to choppy water. Long a windsurf spot, now with kite schools (Freak Winds, Happy Kiter) and described by guides as one of the best kite beaches in Greece. Side-offshore: experienced riders, stay upwind.

name: Epanomi – Potamos
notes: Long sandy beach south of Epanomi village, about 30 min from Thessaloniki; thermal wind in spring and summer, stronger winter winds. A kite school with a rescue boat runs all year (found only on booking sites, no school site).

name: Loutsa (Artemida)
notes: East Attica; meltemi (N–NE) side-shore, chop. Popular Athens spot with schools.

name: Schinias
notes: Long beach in the Marathon bay, partly sheltered from the northerlies. Sources disagree on the wind: one says south winds in the off-season, another a local summer thermal. One small spot to rig and launch, not easy for lessons; a school offers lessons here. Gentle sandy bay for beginners and intermediates in light wind.

name: Theologos
notes: North-west coast near the airport: steady meltemi (N–NW) from about May to October, side-onshore, sandbank with chop and small waves up to about 2 m on strong days; close to shore, so a gentler place to learn than most of the island. Several schools on the beach (Wetskillz IKO centre, Surf & Kite Theologos, Surfin'Bird).

name: Golden Beach (Chrysi Akti)
notes: Long beach on the east coast, about 10 km from Parikia; meltemi (N) side-shore, gusty near the shore, chop. Mainly a windsurf hub (Paros Surf Club, Force 7, Sun Wind) with kite lessons; most guides name Pounta as the main kite area. Busy with bathers: kite in the marked surf zone midway along the beach.

name: Angelochori
notes: Beach at Angelochori west of the airport, with a local summer thermal wind; sand, few waves, all levels, medium crowd. The lagoon behind it is a protected wetland (Natura 2000): keep to the sea side. A windsurf club is on the beach, no kite school found; the nearest is at Epanomi.

name: Chalikounas
notes: Beach between the Korission lagoon and the sea, south-west Corfu: afternoon NW wind from April to September, side-onshore, with some waves. Kite Club Corfu (VDWS station, rescue boat) and a second surf centre on the beach. Korission lagoon behind is a Natura 2000 area: stay on the sea side.

notes: West coast of Rhodes at Fanes, just north of Kalavarda: meltemi (N–NW), May to October, sand and pebble beach. Two kite schools about 100 m away (Meltemi Kiteclub, MKV Kite Station); quieter than the Ixia and Ialyssos coast.

name: Mastichari
notes: North coast of Kos, the island's main kite hub: NNW meltemi side-shore in summer, with an afternoon west thermal that turns onshore; chop and small waves, beginner friendly, May to October. Kite centres on the beach (Horizon Surfing Kos, Kitesurfing Kos) with rescue boats.

name: Amoudara (Heraklion)
notes: North coast of Crete west of Heraklion: NW–NNW meltemi, gusts possible, flat to choppy, all levels, season May to October. iKite (IKO) runs the school here, open June to early September and by appointment outside it.

name: Elafonisi
notes: Lagoon beach at the south-west tip of Crete: steady west wind, very shallow water, scattered rocks; Elafonisi Kite gives lessons here. Protected, busy beach in summer: keep away from swimmers.

name: Ftelia
notes: North coast bay of Mykonos, a beginner-rated kite and windsurf bay in the meltemi (N), May to September. No school found on the beach; the nearest kite school is at Korfos.

name: Kalafati
notes: East coast beach of Mykonos at Kalafati (Agia Anna): listed by guides as an intermediate kite spot, May to September. Single guide source; no school found on the beach.

name: Glyfada
notes: Glyfada Beach on the south-west coast of Naxos, south of Mikri Vigla: meltemi (N) side-shore, mostly flat water good for learning and freestyle, May to September. Described as the island's second kite spot after Mikri Vigla.
